explanation: Ran ./eta/build/exclurad for a single kinematic point: W=1.5576 GeV, Q2=0.5552 GeV2, cos(theta*)=0.651724, phi*=72 deg, with model=3 (EtaMAID2023), rc_mode=0 (full O(alpha) radiative correction, no leading-log approximation), bmom=6.53 GeV, lepton=1 (electron), ivec=1 (recoil proton detected), vcut=0.166 GeV2 -- the standard CLAS12 eta-electroproduction settings documented in eta/README.md. The point is physically valid: it lies above the ep->e'p(eta) threshold (W_thr = m_p+m_eta = 1.486134 GeV) and inside the EtaMAID2023 table grid used for interpolation (Q2 in [0,5] GeV2, W in [1.4856,6] GeV, per eta/mpintp.inc). Note: the exclurad executable hard-codes 'input.dat' as its input filename via an internal OPEN statement (exclurad.F line 39) and ignores stdin redirection, so the point was run by temporarily writing the single-point input to eta/input.dat (saved alongside as eta/input_run1.dat for reproducibility) and afterward restoring the original 10-point template. The run completed normally (exit code 0, no NAG ifail error). Values are read directly, unrounded, from eta/radtot.dat: delta = sigar(1)/sibar(1) (ratio of radiatively-corrected to Born unpolarized cross section) = 0.9159587896; sigma_born = sibar(1) (Born unpolarized cross section in the code's native units, nb-based per the barn=0.389379e6 GeV^-2-to-nb conversion constant in exclurad.F) = 0.0063114262. These are cross-checked by matching values in eta/radcor.dat (0.916) and eta/radsigpl.dat (0.006343, consistent within the quoted precision) and by the stdout convergence line 'test : 0.631E-02 0.631E-02 1.00' confirming the Born-integral cross-check passed.
